idiom_name: readonly properties, readonly T[] / ReadonlyArray and as const; pure functions with explicit types
implementation_notes: TypeScript states the intent in the type system: readonly on a property, Readonly<T>, readonly T[] / ReadonlyArray<T> (which removes push/pop/splice from the type) and as const for literal structures let the compiler reject accidental in-place writes inside a query, and the handbook documents readonly properties as the property modifier that prevents writing. The checks are erased at runtime and they are shallow, so a JavaScript caller, an any cast or a nested mutable object can still break the guarantee - freeze at module boundaries where that matters. Interfaces with setters remain the right shape for entities with identity and lifecycle; keep their mutators as commands.
pitfalls: readonly is compile-time only and shallow: it is erased in the emitted JavaScript, nested objects stay writable, and an any cast or a JavaScript consumer bypasses it completely.
ReadonlyArray parameters remove mutating methods from the type, but many library signatures still take T[], forcing a copy or a cast at the boundary.
as const narrows literals so tightly that ordinary values no longer fit the inferred type; use it for constants, not for data that must accept wider values.
